newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Fudosan to dispose of 200 bln yen in assets.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Fudosan to dispose of 200 bln yen in assets.

text.p: Mitsui Fudosan Co Ltd said on Thursday that it would sell non-performing assets worth about 200 billion yen in the latter half of the 1996/97 fiscal year ending next March at a loss of about 110 billion yen.

However, it also expects to raise special profits of 27.6 billion yen stemming from the sale of 5.5 million shares it owns in Oriental Land Co Ltd, the operator of Tokyo Disneyland, in the latter half, offsetting the part of the losses from the non-performing asset sales, it said in a statement.
Mitsui said earlier it would post 70.3 billion yen in parent current loss and 73.8 billion yen in parent net loss for the financial year to next March as a result of the disposal of bad assets.
However, it said in a statement that the company expects an overall profit in 1997/98 because of more than 45 billion yen in parent operating profit on parent sales of more than 600 billion yen.
Mitsui said the company plans to cut its debt on which it has to make interest payments from the current 1.26 trillion yen because the amount of the debt is excessive.

Through disposing of unprofitable assets which the company had bought in the late 1980s "bubble economy" of inflated stock and land prices, it targets a cutback of the debt just below one trillion yen over the next two years, Mitsui said.

The sales of bad assets worth 200 billion yen on a book value for 1996/97 means Mitsui needs to cut the debt by another 100 billion yen in 1997/98, it said, adding that the company plans to sell assets with a book value of 110 billion yen in the next financial year to achieve the targets.
Analysts said Mitsui Fudosan had been well expected to sell shares in Oriental Land in 1996/97 in order to cover losses stemming from the sale of unprofitable real estate.
"It is positive news for Mitsui Fudosan shares," said Hirokazu Nihei, an analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd.

"Most of Mitsui Fudosan's non-performing assets will be disposed of (in 1996/97), and I think the worst of its non-performing asset problem is over from its decision to post losses (in 1996/97)," he said.
Mitsui Fudosan is a major real estate company in Japan, developing residential condominiums and commercial buildings.
